64:1: God Almighty says: Whatever is in the seven heavens and whatever is on the earth of His creation prostrates to Him and glorifies Him. And His saying: To Him belongs the kingdom, God Almighty says: To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and His authority is complete. His judgment is binding on them and His command is carried out. And His statement: And to Him be praise means: To Him be praise for all of the creation in it, because all of the creation in it does not know good except from Him, and they have no provider other than Him, so to Him be praise of all of them. And He is over all things competent means He is over all things competent, possessing power. He says: He creates what He wills, causes to die whom He wills, enriches whom He wills, impoverishes whom He wills, honors whom He wills, and humiliates whom He wills. Nothing He wills is impossible for Him, because He is the Possessor of complete power with which nothing is impossible for Him.
64:2: God Almighty says: God is the One who created you O people, and He is the One who mentioned the name of God so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer He says: So among you is a disbeliever in his Creator and that He created him, and among you is a believer: He says: And among you is he who believes in Him and is certain that He is his Creator or Originator And God is Seeing of what you do He says: And God who created you is Seeing of your deeds and Knowing of them, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for them, so fear Him lest you disobey Him in His commands and prohibitions, lest He transgress against you. Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi told us: Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashib told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told us: Bakr ibn Sawada told us, on the authority of Abu Tamim al-Jaishani, on the authority of Abu Dharr: When the semen remains in the womb for forty nights, it comes to the Angel of Souls and ascends with it to the Almighty in His palm. He says: O Lord, is this servant of yours male or female? Then God decrees for him what He will decree, then he says: O Lord, am I miserable or happy? Then He writes down what he will encounter. He said: Abu Dharr recited the opening chapter of al-Taghabun, five verses.
64:3: God Almighty says: He created the seven heavens and the earth with justice and fairness, and He formed you. He says: And likened you and made your likeness perfect. It was said that by that He meant His forming of Adam and creating him with His hand. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He created the heavens and the earth in truth and formed you and perfected your forms, meaning Adam, whom He created with His own hand. And His saying: And to Him is the return means: And to God is the return of all of you, O people.
64:4: God Almighty says: Your Lord knows, O people, whatever is in the seven heavens and the earth. Nothing of that is hidden from Him. And He knows what you conceal, O people, among yourselves, of word and deed, and what you declare, of that and reveal it. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts. God Almighty says: God has knowledge of the innermost thoughts of His servants, and what their souls conceal, which is more hidden than a secret. Nothing of that escapes Him. God Almighty says, because of His distance: Beware of concealing something other than what you declare, or concealing within yourselves something other than what you reveal, for nothing of that is hidden from your Lord. He is the preserver of all of it, and He is the guardian of all of it.
64:5: God Almighty says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:“Has there not come to you, O people, the report of those who disbelieved before you, such as the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, and the people of Lot? “And they tasted the evil consequences of their deed.” So God’s punishment touched them for their disbelief. And for them is a painful punishment. He says: And for them is a painful, agonizing punishment on the Day of Resurrection in the fire of Hell, along with what God made them taste in this world for the evil consequences of their disbelief.
64:6: And His statement: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, God, the Most High, says: This is what befell those who disbelieved before these polytheists as a result of their disbelief, and what their Lord has prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection of punishment, because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs whom their Lord sent with clear evidence and signs of the truth of what they were calling them to. So they said to them: Are human beings guiding us? Out of arrogance on their part that God's messengers to them were human beings like them and out of arrogance about following the truth because a human being like them called them to it. And the report was made plural from the human beings, so it was said: They guide us, and He did not say: He guides us, because human beings, even though it is in the singular form, still means all. And His statement: But they disbelieved and turned away. He says: So they disbelieved in God and rejected the message of His Messengers whom God sent to them out of arrogance. And they turned away. He says: And they turned away from the truth and did not accept it, and they turned away from what their Messengers called them to. And God was independent of them. He says: God was independent of them and of their belief in Him and in His Messenger, and they had no need of Him for that. And God is Free of need, Praiseworthy. He says: God is independent of all of His creation, praised by all of them for His beautiful favors toward them, and His noble deeds toward them.
64:7: God Almighty says: Those who disbelieved in God claimed that God would not resurrect them from their graves after their death. Ibn Omar used to say: He claimed a false nickname. Muhammad bin Nafi’ al-Basri told me this. He said: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ibn Umar. And His statement: “Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected.” He is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them, O Muhammad: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected from your graves. Then you will surely be informed of what you did. He says: Then you will be informed of the deeds that you did in this world. And that is easy for God. He says: And your resurrection from your graves after your death is easy and simple for God.
64:8: God the Almighty says: So believe in God and His Messenger, you polytheists who deny the Resurrection, and in His informing you that you will be resurrected after your death, and that after your trials you will be raised from your graves, and the light which We have sent down meaning: And believe in the light which We have sent down, which is this Qur’an that God sent down to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And God is Acquainted with what you do meaning: God the Almighty says: And God, O people, is All-Knowing of your deeds, encompassing them, measuring them all, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of them.
64:9: God Almighty says: And God is All-Knowing of what you do. The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly of all creation for display. That is the Day of Loss. He says: The assembly is the day when the people of Paradise will lose the people of Hell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, That is the Day of Loss, he said: It is the loss of the people of Paradise by the people of Hell. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, The Day He will gather you for the Day of Assembly is the Day of Resurrection, and it is the Day of Loss: the Day the people of Paradise will be deceived by the people of Hell. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, That is the Day of Loss, one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, he glorified it and warned his servants about it. And His statement: And whoever believes in God and does righteousness, God Almighty says: And whoever believes in God and acts in obedience to Him, and adheres to His commands and prohibitions, He will remove from him his misdeeds, meaning, He will erase his sins, and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, meaning, He will admit him to orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow. His saying: They will abide therein forever means: They will remain therein forever, they will not die, nor will they leave it. His saying: That is the great attainment means: Their eternity in the gardens that we have described is the great salvation.
64:10: God Almighty says: And those who denied the Oneness of God, and rejected His proofs and arguments and the verses of His Book which He sent down to His servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. He says: They will remain therein forever, they will never die, nor will they leave it. And wretched is the destination. He says: And wretched is the thing to which one will be led: Hell.
64:11: God Almighty says: No calamity befalls anyone except by God’s permission, meaning: except by God’s decree and predestination for him. And whoever believes in God - He will guide his heart. Meaning: And whoever believes in God and knows that no one is afflicted with a calamity except by God’s permission, thereby He guides his heart. Meaning: God will guide his heart to submit to His command and be content with His decree. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And whoever believes in God - He guides his heart, meaning: He guides his heart to certainty, so he knows that what befell him could not have missed him, and what missed him could not have befallen him. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Washa Al-Awdi told me: Ahmad bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhabiyan, who said: We were with Alqamah, and this verse was recited to him: And whoever believes in God - He will guide his heart. He was asked about that, and he said: It is a man who is afflicted with a calamity, and he knows that it is from God, so he accepts that and is satisfied. Isa bin Othman Al-Ramli told me: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhabiyan, who said: I was with Alqamah while he was reviewing the copies of the Qur’an, and he passed by this verse: “No disaster strikes except by permission of God. And whoever believes in God - He will guide his heart.” He said: He is the man... then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amir told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Alqamah, regarding His statement: “No disaster strikes except by permission of God. And whoever believes in God - He will guide his heart.” He said: It is the man who is struck by a disaster, and he knows that it is from God, so he submits to it and is content with it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Mahdi told me, on the authority of Al-Thawri, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Alqamah, the same, except that he said in his hadith, so he knows that it is from the decree of God, so he is satisfied with it and submits. And His saying: And God is All-Knowing of everything means: God has knowledge of everything, of what was, what will be, and what will be before it came to be.
64:12: God Almighty says: And obey God O people, in His commands and prohibitions and obey the Messenger may God bless him and grant him peace but if you turn away “if you turn away from obeying God and obeying His Messenger, being arrogant about it, and do not obey God or His Messenger” then there is nothing upon our Messenger” Muhammad except the clear conveyance that he conveyed to you what I sent him with. He, the Most High, says: He has excused you for conveying, and God is the Guardian of vengeance against whoever disobeys Him, opposes His command, and turns away from him.
64:13: God, there is no god but Him. The Most High says: Your God, O people, is one God. Worship is not appropriate for anyone other than Him, and you have no other god but Him. And in God let the believers put their trust. God Almighty says: And in God, O people, let those who believe in His Oneness put their trust.
64:14: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you who turn you away from the path of God and discourage you from obeying God. So beware of them that you do not accept from them what they command you to do of abandoning the obedience of God. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about a people who wanted to convert to Islam and emigrate, but their wives and children discouraged them from doing so. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated: Yahya bin Adam and Ubaydullah bin Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man asked him about this verse: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. He said: These are men who had embraced Islam and wanted to go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but their wives and children refused to let them go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). When they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), they saw that the people had acquired understanding of the religion, and they intended to punish them. Then God, the Most High, revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children… Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated: Abu Al-Ahwas narrated to us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the statement of God, O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them, he said: A man wanted to go to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his family would say to him, Where are you going and leaving us? He said, If he converts to Islam and is guided, I will return to those who forbade this matter, and I will do this and that. Then God, the Most High, revealed, But if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. When a man wanted to migrate from Mecca to Medina, his wife and children would prevent him, and they would spare no effort to discourage him from doing so. Then God said, They are your enemies, so beware of them, and listen and obey, and go about your business. After that, if a man was prevented or discouraged, he would go to his family and swear – and an oath is an oath – that they would do it and that he would punish his family for that. Then God, the Most High, said, But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated: Some of his companions narrated: Ata ibn Yasar said: The entirety of Surat At-Taghabun was revealed in Mecca, except for these verses: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. It was revealed about Awf ibn Malik Al-Ashja’i, who had a family and children. Whenever he wanted to go out for a military expedition, they would weep for him and show compassion, saying: To whom are you leaving us? He would be compassionate and stay put. Then the verse: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. was revealed in Medina. The entire verse was about Awf ibn Malik, and the rest of the verses to the end of the surah were in Medina. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them, he said: They will lead him to sever his family ties and to disobey his Lord, and despite his love for them, he will have no choice but to sever them. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: So he cannot do anything but obey Him despite his love. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them... the verse. He said: Among them are those who do not command obedience to God, nor forbid disobedience, and they were slow to migrate to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to engage in jihad. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them, he said: They forbid Islam and are slow to convert to it, and they are among the disbelievers, so beware of them. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you… the verse, this was about people from the Arab tribes. A man or a group of people would convert to Islam from their clans, so they would leave their clans and call upon their wives, children and fathers, heading to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Their clans, wives, children and fathers would stand up and implore them by God not to leave them and not to prefer anyone else over them. Some of them would take pity on them and return to them, and some would go on until they joined the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Kurayb narrated: Uthman bin Najiyah and Zayd bin Habbab narrated: Yahya bin Wadhah narrated to us, both of them, on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Waqid, who narrated: Abdullah bin Buraidah narrated to me, on the authority of his father, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivering a sermon, and Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, came wearing two red shirts, stumbling and standing up. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came down, took them, lifted them up, and put them in a room, then said: God and His Messenger have spoken the truth: Your wealth and your children are but a trial. I saw these two and I could not be patient. Then he began his sermon. The wording is from Abu Kurayb on the authority of Zayd. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, he said: He says: An enemy to you in your religion, so beware of them in your religion. Muhammad bin Amr bin Ali Al-Muqaddami told me: Ash’ath bin Abdullah told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, regarding his statement, Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. He said: A man would convert to Islam, and his family and children would blame him, so the verse, Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you was revealed. And His statement, But if you pardon and overlook, means: And if you pardon, O believers, what happened in the past from them in preventing you from Islam and emigration, and overlook your punishment of them for that, and forgive them other sins, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful to you, to whoever of His servants repents from your sins, Merciful to you, that He does not punish you for them after you have repented from them.
64:15: God Almighty says: Your wealth and your children, O people, are nothing but a trial, meaning a calamity for you in this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who told you: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Your wealth and your children are only a trial, meaning a calamity. And His saying: And God has with Him a great reward means: God has with Him a great reward for you, if you disobey your children and wives in obeying God, your Lord, and obey God Almighty, and fulfill God’s right in your wealth, and the great reward that is with God is Paradise. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And God has a great reward with Him, which is Paradise.
64:16: And His statement: So fear God as much as you are able, God Almighty says: O believers, beware of God and fear His punishment, and avoid His torment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins, and doing what brings you closer to Him, as much as you are able and within your means. He mentioned that his saying, So fear God as much as you are able, was revealed after his saying, Fear God as He should be feared (Al Imran 3:102), to make things easier for the Muslims, and that his saying, So fear God as much as you are able abrogates his saying, Fear God as He should be feared (Al Imran 3:102). Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, So fear God as much as you are able, and listen and obey, this is a dispensation from God, and God is Merciful to His servants. God, the Most High, had previously revealed, Fear God as He should be feared (Al Imran 3:102), and the right to fear Him means that He should be obeyed and not disobeyed. Then God, the Most High, made it easier for His servants to remember Him, so He revealed the dispensation after that, saying, So fear God as much as you are able, and listen and obey, so as much as you are able, O son of Adam. Upon this, the Messenger of God pledged allegiance to hear and obey as much as you are able. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Fear God as He should be feared (Al Imran 3:102), he said: It was abrogated by Fear God as much as you are able. We have already explained the meaning of the abrogating and the abrogated in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. There is no clear indication in His statement, So fear God as much as you are able, that it is abrogating, since it was possible that he said, Fear God as much as you are able, and it was not that it was abrogated by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If that is the case, then it is obligatory to use them all according to the aspects of validity that they both bear. His statement, And listen and obey, means: And listen to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and obey him in what he commands you to do and what he forbids you from doing. And spend for yourselves what is good, means: And spend money from your wealth for yourselves to save them from God’s punishment. Good in this context means money. And His statement: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. God Almighty says: And whoever God protects from the stinginess of his soul, which is following his desires in what God has forbidden. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, meaning: the desires of his soul, where he follows his desires and does not accept faith. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jami’ ibn Shaddad, on the authority of Al-Aswad ibn Hilal, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud: And whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul he said: that he should take someone else’s money and consume it. And His saying: Those are the successful ones, meaning: These are the ones who have been protected from their own greed, the successful ones who have achieved their requests from their Lord.
64:17: God Almighty says: “And if you spend in the cause of God, spending well therein, and expecting reward from your spending, your Lord will multiply it for you, giving you seven hundred times more, or even more than that, as He wills, and forgive you your sins, pardoning you for them, while doubling your spending in His cause. And God is Most Appreciative.” He says: God is Most Appreciative of those who spend in His cause, by rewarding them well for what they spent in this world in His cause. Forbearing. He says: Forbearing towards those who disobey Him, by not hastening His punishment upon them.
64:18: The Knower of the Unseen and the Seen He says: He knows what the eyes of His servants do not see and what is hidden from their sight and what they witness but see with their sight. The Mighty means the Severe in His vengeance against those who disobey Him and violate His commands and prohibitions. The Wise in His management of His creation, of them in what is best for them.
